raw_text:
The research objective is to understand why repeated responses to the same question may vary and identify observable factors contributing to this variation, using a Bayesian methodological approach. The scope includes examining individual and environmental factors that might influence repeat responses.

Assumptions
- Individuals may provide different responses to the same question over time due to changes in their attitudes, knowledge, or external influences.
- Observable factors such as time since last response, emotional state, or environmental context can affect repeat responses.
- Prior beliefs about potential factors can guide the probabilistic nature of Bayesian inference.

Research design
- We will use a longitudinal survey design, collecting repeated responses over time from a diverse sample of individuals.
- A Bayesian hierarchical model will be employed to account for within and between-person variability.

Data or evidence needed
- Repeated responses to the same question from multiple occasions per person.
- Demographic and situational data (e.g., time since last response, emotional state rating) for each respondent and response.
- Historical data about similar studies or relevant theories to inform prior distributions.

Measurement
- The primary outcome measure is the consistency of responses to a fixed question across repeated measures.
- Questionnaire items will be used to assess demographic variables and potential influencing factors (e.g., emotional state, external events).

Analysis
- Bayesian hierarchical models will be fitted to estimate the distribution of both individual and environmental factors affecting response consistency.
- Posterior predictive checks will be used to evaluate model fit and check for overfitting.
- The model will allow us to derive credible intervals for parameter estimates and assess the likelihood of competing explanations.

Decision / stopping rule
- The study will run for a predetermined period (e.g., one year) or until we reach a fixed sample size of complete datasets.
- Data evaluation will occur at monthly intervals to ensure the quality and relevancy of data collection and model adjustments.

Limitations
- Self-reported data may introduce biases related to social desirability or memory effects.
- External events affecting individuals over the study period may not be fully captured or controlled for.
